title: Asia-Pacific Geopolitics and India's Maritime Strategy

scenes.text: Why are world superpowers competing to control the South China Sea?
scenes.narration: Imagine a single sea carrying over five trillion dollars in trade every year. The country that commands these waters can shape the future of global power!

scenes.text: A shared school corridor must stay open for everyone, not blocked by one bully.
scenes.narration: Here is an everyday analogy to make this click. Think of the ocean like your school corridor; if one student blocks the passage, nobody else can reach their classroom safely.

scenes.heading: From Look East to Act East
scenes.narration: India upgraded its old Look East policy into Act East. Rather than just trading with Southeast Asia, India now secures vital shipping lanes across the wider Indo-Pacific.

scenes.name: Robert D. Kaplan
scenes.idea: South China Sea is the future geopolitical hotspot of conflict.
scenes.narration: Scholar Robert Kaplan warned that the South China Sea is the new global hotspot. Just like Europe in World War Two, major powers clash here over shipping lanes and artificial islands.

scenes.heading: The Risk of Chinese Loans
scenes.narration: Here's the trick to understanding China's Belt and Road project. When borrowing nations cannot repay high-interest loans, China can demand strategic land swaps, threatening their national sovereignty.

scenes.heading: India's Maritime and OBOR Stand
items: Rejects CPEC to defend territorial sovereignty
Protects sea routes as net security provider
Promotes alternatives like Japan's Quality Infrastructure
scenes.narration: India refused to join China's project because it violates our sovereignty. Instead, India acts as a net security provider, meaning it helps protect neighboring waters from threats while partnering with friends like Japan.

items: South China Sea is a critical trade hotspot
Act East expands India's naval security role
India rejects OBOR to safeguard sovereignty
scenes.narration: To ace your exam, remember these three core ideas. Control over Asian seas is reshaping global diplomacy, and India is firmly safeguarding its sovereignty.
